newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT- Stg to consolidate above 2.9480 mark low.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT- Stg to consolidate above 2.9480 mark low.

text.p: The pound will consolidate above Tuesday's low of 2.9480 marks after its spurt to fresh six-year highs yesterday before attempting a push to the psychological barrier at 3.00, technical analysts said.
Sterling surged to a high of 2.9758 marks on Tuesday and also rose to a new near-seven month peak against the dollar at $1.6956.
Technically, the pound looks flat and with the two-day Bank of England monetary policy committee meeting starting today, traders expect the currency to be rangebound intraday.
At 0730 GMT sterling was at 2.9665/75 marks and $1.6868/78.
That compared with 2.9730/40 and $1.6900/10 in late European trading on Tuesday.

"Sterling remains in an uptrend against both the mark and the dollar but there is scope for consolidation before it heads higher again," said Stefan Steinemann, technical analyst at Lloyds Bank in Geneva.

Sterling/mark faces little resistance on the way to 3.00 marks apart from an initial barrier at 2.98, said Steinemann. Above 2.98 marks, sterling would be eyeing 2.9825, its highest since late May 1991.
Hans-Guenter Redeker, technical analyst at Chase, said sterling would continue to move higher in the short term, provided that corrective setbacks maintain levels above 2.9480.
The 3.00 mark level is psychologically important but technically, trendline resistances at 3.0170 and 3.0280 are more important, chartists said.
Cable looked well supported at $1.6810/20, said Steinemann who expects a move to a target at $1.72 in the near term. That would push the pound to levels not seen since October 1992.
"A loss of $1.6810/20 would increase the risk of a drop to $1.67 before going up again but I think cable can go higher directly," said Steinemann.
First resistance was at $1.6960, around the Tuesday high, with $1.70 posing a psychological barrier.
Redeker at Chase noted that since the March 18 low of $1.5858 the pound had continued to make higher highs and higher lows.
"The June 23 breakout above the 1.6965 level has improved the technical outlook further, confirming that a major bottom is in place at the 1.5858 low," said Redeker.
